instruction: Open the workspace file /home/user/workspace1.code-workspace in VS Code.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VS Code settings, navigated File > Open Workspace from File, successfully opened workspace1.code-workspace, attempted to add workspace2 folders, then correctly identified opening two workspaces in the same window as infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VS Code menus, open workspace files via File dialog, use keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+`, F1, Ctrl+Shift+P), interact with file manager, understand VS Code workspace limitations
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified the original infeasible task to just opening a single workspace, which the model demonstrated it can do in the trajectory
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening workspace1.code-workspace in VS Code. Evaluator checks VS Code window title contains 'workspace1 (Workspace)' using wmctrl/xdotool.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses wmctrl/xdotool to extract VS Code window titles, which is the appropriate method for checking window state on Linux

Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule': expected IS the rules dict {'keyword': 'workspace1 (Workspace)'}, and the metric accesses expected.get('keyword') directly - correct pattern
Expected keyword 'workspace1 (Workspace)' matches VS Code's actual title bar format when a .code-workspace file is opened
Case-insensitive substring matching is appropriate and robust for title comparison
Single instruction requirement (open workspace file) is fully covered by the single evaluator check (window title contains workspace name)
Postconfig includes a 1-second sleep to allow window title to update after workspace opens
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The getter could benefit from a slightly longer timeout or retry logic in case VS Code is slow to update its window title, but this is not a blocking issue
